questions.stem: What prevents the atrioventricular valves from turning inside out when the ventricles contract?

options.text: The thick muscular walls of the ventricles
Tendons (chordae tendineae) attached to papillary muscles
The semilunar valves closing at the same time
The pressure of blood in the atria

questions.explanation: The chordae tendineae are tendons that attach the valve flaps to papillary muscles in the ventricle wall, preventing the valves from inverting under the high pressure of ventricular contraction.
